Tailcat connection

Source: R/connection.R
TailcatConnection.Rd

A TCP stream or connected UDP flow between a TailcatClient and a TailcatServer. Connections are created by TailcatClient$dial() and TailcatListener$accept(), not directly.

For TCP, reads may return fewer bytes than requested and $read() returns NULL at end of stream. For UDP, each read returns one datagram (possibly raw(0)) and each write sends one datagram of at most 1232 bytes (tailcat_udp_max_payload()). $write_message() and $read_message() send and receive delimited messages over TCP (see the section on messages), and $read_loop() reads continuously from the event loop (see the section on read loops).

One read and one write may be in flight at the same time (for example a pending $read_async() while writing). Further operations in the same direction wait their turn and run in the order they were started, for synchronous and asynchronous calls alike, so several $write_async() calls send their data in call order and several $read_async() calls receive consecutive chunks of the stream in call order. The wait counts toward each operation's timeout, and canceling or timing out an operation that is still waiting ends it without affecting the others.

$client or $server (the other is NULL) gives the object that owns the connection, the client that dialed it or the server whose listener accepted it.

Once the connection, or the client or server that owns it, is closed, every method other than $close(), $format(), and $print(), and every field other than $is_closed, $client, and $server, raises a tailcat_closed error; nothing is kept from before. Timeouts (including timeout = 0, a poll) and errors are described in TailcatServer.

Because of an upstream tailcat bug, $info() (and so $local_address and $remote_address) fails with tailcat_failure, and the Go runtime prints a stack trace to standard error, on a TCP connection whose two directions have both been shut down (both sides called $close_write()). $print() and $format() avoid this by leaving the endpoints out once $close_write() has succeeded on the connection.

Messages

TCP is a stream of bytes with no boundaries: one $write() may arrive as several reads, and several writes as one. $write_message() and $read_message() add boundaries, so that each $read_message() returns exactly what one $write_message() sent. On the wire a message is its length as 4 bytes (unsigned, big-endian, so a peer in another language can implement it in a few lines) followed by that many bytes. The protocol allows messages up to 4 GiB; rtailcat sends and accepts at most 2147483647 bytes (just under 2 GiB) per message.

Give $read_message() a max_bytes that fits your protocol whenever the peer is not fully trusted: the length is checked before the message is read, so an oversized message is refused without reading it into memory.

To send R objects, serialize them: conn$write_message(serialize(x, NULL)) and unserialize(conn$read_message(max_bytes = 1e8)). Only do this with peers you trust completely: unserialize() on data from an untrusted peer can run arbitrary code. Use a data format such as JSON otherwise.

Read loops

$read_loop(callback) reads continuously, driven by the later event loop, and calls callback(data) on the main R thread with each chunk (TCP), each datagram (UDP), or with messages = TRUE each message. It is the reading counterpart of TailcatListener$serve() and makes progress under the same conditions: while R is idle at the console, inside Shiny or httpuv, or while a script runs the event loop (see tailcat_run()). If callback returns a promise, the next read starts after it settles, so data is handled in order and a slow callback slows down reading rather than piling up work.

The loop ends when the peer ends a TCP stream (on_end is then called), when the connection or its owner is closed, or when $stop_reading() is called; the last two end it quietly. If a read fails or the callback fails, on_error is called, the loop stops, and the connection is closed. While a read loop runs, other reads on the connection would interleave with it, so only write.

Active bindings

local_address

The local endpoint as "host:port" on the tailcat network. It is fetched from tailcat on each access.

remote_address

The peer's endpoint as "host:port" on the tailcat network. It is fetched from tailcat on each access.

network

"tcp" or "udp".

client

The TailcatClient that dialed the connection, or NULL for an accepted connection. Like $server, it keeps working after the connection is closed.

server

The TailcatServer whose listener accepted the connection, or NULL for a dialed connection. It keeps working after the connection is closed.

is_closed

TRUE once the connection, or the client or server that owns it, has been closed.

TailcatConnection$read()

Read up to n bytes (TCP) or one datagram (UDP, truncated to n bytes). One call returns at most 65536 bytes whatever the value of n (TCP reads may return less than requested anyway, and UDP datagrams are much smaller), so loop, or use $read_all(), to read more. A timeout ends only this read; the connection stays usable. With timeout = 0 the read returns data (or the end of stream) that has already arrived, and otherwise raises tailcat_timeout at once. A TCP read returns whatever has arrived, so with as = "text" a multibyte UTF-8 character can be split across two reads; for multibyte text use $read_all(), or read raw bytes and convert them once. On UDP, n = 0 is not supported: because of an upstream tailcat bug it fails and the datagram is lost.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read(n = 65536L, timeout = Inf, as = c("raw", "text"))

Arguments

n

Maximum number of bytes to return (at most 65536 are returned).

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

as

Exactly "raw" (the default) to return a raw vector, or "text" to return a single string marked as UTF-8 (the bytes are not checked for valid UTF-8). Data containing NUL bytes cannot be returned as text and raises a tailcat_invalid_argument error; the data is consumed, so read binary data with as = "raw".

Returns

A raw vector or a string, or NULL at TCP end of stream.

TailcatConnection$read_all()

Read until the peer ends the stream (TCP only). On timeout or error the condition's bytes field gives the number of bytes read before it; those bytes are discarded. With timeout = 0 it returns only if the whole stream, including its end, has already arrived.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read_all(
  timeout = Inf,
  as = c("raw", "text"),
  max_bytes = Inf
)

Arguments

timeout

Overall seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

as

Exactly "raw" (the default) to return a raw vector, or "text" to return a single string marked as UTF-8 ("" for an empty stream). See $read() for NUL bytes.

max_bytes

The most bytes to accept, a single non-negative whole number or Inf (the default) for no limit. If the stream is longer, reading stops after max_bytes + 1 bytes and a tailcat_failure error is raised whose bytes field is the number of bytes read (max_bytes + 1). Those bytes are discarded, but the connection stays open and usable: the rest of the stream can still be read, or the connection closed.

Returns

A raw vector or a string.

TailcatConnection$read_all_async()

Asynchronous version of $read_all(). Canceling the promise with tailcat_cancel() ends the read in flight and starts no further reads.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read_all_async(
  timeout = Inf,
  as = c("raw", "text"),
  max_bytes = Inf
)

Arguments

timeout

Overall seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

as

"raw" or "text", as for $read_all().

max_bytes

The most bytes to accept, as for $read_all(); a longer stream rejects the promise with a tailcat_failure error.

Returns

A promise resolving with a raw vector or a string.

TailcatConnection$read_exact()

Read exactly n bytes (TCP only), waiting for as many reads as that takes. Use it to read fixed-size fields of a binary protocol; for messages of varying length see $read_message().

If the stream ends before the first byte, $read_exact() returns NULL, so a peer that closes the connection between records is not an error. If it ends part way, or on timeout or error, the condition's bytes field gives the number of bytes read before it; those bytes are discarded. The timeout covers all the reads together. With timeout = 0 it returns only if all n bytes have already arrived.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read_exact(n, timeout = Inf, as = c("raw", "text"))

Arguments

n

The number of bytes to read, a single non-negative whole number. n = 0 returns raw(0) (or "") without reading.

timeout

Overall seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

as

"raw" or "text", as for $read().

Returns

A raw vector or a string of n bytes, or NULL if the stream ended before the first byte.

TailcatConnection$read_exact_async()

Asynchronous version of $read_exact(). Canceling the promise with tailcat_cancel() ends the read in flight and starts no further reads.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read_exact_async(n, timeout = Inf, as = c("raw", "text"))

timeout

as

Returns

A promise resolving with a raw vector or a string, or NULL if the stream ended before the first byte.

TailcatConnection$write_message()

Send data as one message (TCP only), for the peer to read with $read_message(). See the section on messages.

Usage

TailcatConnection$write_message(data, timeout = Inf)

Arguments

data

A raw vector, or a character vector which is pasted together without separators and sent as UTF-8. At most 2147483647 bytes.

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls. On timeout or error the condition's bytes field gives the number of bytes already sent, counting the 4-byte length; the peer then sees a partial message, so close the connection.

Returns

The number of bytes in the message, not counting its length prefix, invisibly.

Arguments

A raw or character vector.

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

Returns

A promise resolving with the number of bytes in the message.

TailcatConnection$read_message()

Read one message sent with $write_message() (TCP only). See the section on messages.

If the stream ends cleanly between messages, $read_message() returns NULL. If it ends part way through a message, or on timeout or error, the condition's bytes field gives the number of bytes read, counting the 4-byte length; those bytes are discarded and the connection should be closed, since the rest of the stream no longer starts at a message boundary. The timeout covers the whole message.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read_message(
  timeout = Inf,
  as = c("raw", "text"),
  max_bytes = Inf
)

Arguments

timeout

Overall seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

as

"raw" or "text", as for $read().

max_bytes

The largest message to accept, a single non-negative whole number or Inf (the default; messages are limited to 2147483647 bytes in any case). The length is checked before the message is read: a longer message raises a tailcat_failure error with bytes set to 4, and its body is left unread, so close the connection.

Returns

A raw vector or a string, or NULL if the stream ended before the next message.

TailcatConnection$read_message_async()

Asynchronous version of $read_message(). Canceling the promise with tailcat_cancel() ends the read in flight and starts no further reads; a message read part way is lost.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read_message_async(
  timeout = Inf,
  as = c("raw", "text"),
  max_bytes = Inf
)

Arguments

timeout

Overall seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

as

"raw" or "text", as for $read().

max_bytes

The largest message to accept, as for $read_message().

Returns

A promise resolving with a raw vector or a string, or NULL if the stream ended before the next message.

TailcatConnection$read_loop()

Start an asynchronous read loop that calls callback(data) with every chunk (TCP), datagram (UDP), or message (with messages = TRUE) as it arrives, and returns immediately. See the section on read loops.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read_loop(
  callback,
  on_error = NULL,
  on_end = NULL,
  as = c("raw", "text"),
  messages = FALSE,
  max_bytes = Inf
)

Arguments

callback

A function of one argument, the data read. It may return a promise, in which case the next read starts once the promise settles.

on_error

A function function(cond) called when a read fails, the data is not acceptable (such as a message longer than max_bytes), callback signals an error, or the promise it returned rejects; or NULL to turn such errors into warnings (signaled from the later event loop). The loop then stops and the connection is closed. An error signaled by on_error itself is turned into a warning.

on_end

A function of no arguments called when the peer ends a TCP stream, after the last data, or NULL. An error it signals is turned into a warning.

as

"raw" or "text", as for $read().

messages

FALSE (the default) to deliver data as it arrives, or TRUE to deliver whole messages sent with $write_message() (TCP only).

max_bytes

The largest message to accept with messages = TRUE, as for $read_message().

Returns

The connection, invisibly. Calling it on a connection that is already in a read loop raises a tailcat_failure error (call $stop_reading() first), and on a closed connection a tailcat_closed error.

TailcatConnection$stop_reading()

Stop the read loop started by $read_loop() without closing the connection. The pending read is canceled; data whose read completed at the same moment is still passed to the callback, but a message read part way is lost, so with messages = TRUE stop only between messages or then close the connection. Calling it when no read loop is running does nothing.

Usage

TailcatConnection$stop_reading()

Returns

The connection, invisibly.

TailcatConnection$format()

Format a summary, the lines that $print() shows. An open connection shows its local and remote endpoints on the tailcat network (not secrets); they are left out when the connection is closed, when tailcat cannot report them, and once $close_write() has succeeded on it, because asking tailcat after both sides have shut down their writes triggers an upstream bug that prints a Go stack trace.

Usage

TailcatConnection$format(...)

Arguments

...

Ignored.

Returns

A character vector.

TailcatConnection$print()

Print the summary from $format().

Usage

TailcatConnection$print(...)

Arguments

...

Ignored.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn = TailcatClient$new(address)$dial(8080)
conn$write("ping")
conn$close_write()
conn$read_all(timeout = 10, as = "text")
} # }
